parity_risks: STICKY CACHED STATE: `cached`, `rows`/`items`/`keys`/`animating`, `last_painted`, `offset`, `selected_key` all persist across ticks. Input at the TOP of a tick is deliberately handled against the PREVIOUS build's rows/keys/items (comment sidebar.py:981-982); a forced poll later in the same tick rebuilds them. A Rust port that rebuilds eagerly before dispatching input breaks the invariant that indices are valid and that Enter/click acts on what is on screen.

REDRAW GATING BY VALUE EQUALITY: `dirty = input_detected or (frame_advanced and animating) or snapshot != last_painted` where `snapshot = (cached, selected_key)` and `cached` is a 7-tuple containing the whole windows list, sessions list, pane_progress/pane_status maps, and has_focus (sidebar.py:1093, 1119-1120). Python compares these DEEPLY by value. Rust must derive structural PartialEq over the entire snapshot (or an equivalent content hash), NOT pointer identity, or an idle sidebar will busy-repaint or fail to repaint on data change. `has_focus` is inside `cached`, so a focus-only change repaints via this diff without any keypress.

BUILD GATING: build_rows runs ONLY when `polled or (frame_advanced and animating)` (sidebar.py:1108). `animating` is computed from the PREVIOUS build (any on-screen indicator glyph in the braille spinner set, sidebar.py:1117). So a spinner keeps animating only because the last build had one on screen; the first spinner appears on a poll, which flips `animating` true, and subsequent frame advances then rebuild. Getting this ordering wrong yields either a frozen spinner or a rebuild-every-tick regression.

SPAWN-RACE SINGLETON: self-exit compares `int(p[1:]) < int(SIDEBAR_PANE[1:])` (sidebar.py:1027) — pane ids are like `%12`; the compare is NUMERIC on the integer after stripping `%`, not lexical string compare. Lexical compare ("%2" vs "%12") would pick the wrong survivor.

MONOTONIC SCHEDULING: last_poll/last_frame start at 0.0 and force_poll starts True, so the first tick always polls AND advances a frame. Use a monotonic clock (time.monotonic equivalent), never wall-clock, for POLL_INTERVAL(1.0s)/ANIM_INTERVAL(0.0625s); TICK_MS=16 is the getch timeout and the repaint ceiling (at most one repaint per tick).

keys.index(selected_key) finds the FIRST occurrence (sidebar.py:989,992,995). Selection keys must be unique tuples; an agent key is ("a", session_id, pane) with pane included precisely so a session placed under several windows stays unique. Port must reproduce first-match semantics and key shape exactly.

EMPTY-LISTS GUARD: nav/enter/mouse branches are gated on `keys and`/`rows and`/`items` (sidebar.py:988,991,994,996). On the very first tick these are empty so keys do nothing until the first build. Do not let a Rust port panic on index into empty lists or act before the first poll.

selected_key RECONCILIATION: after a build, if selected_key is not in keys it snaps to the first active-window row else keys[0] (sidebar.py:1113-1116). This runs only inside need_build; between builds selected_key may reference a stale-but-still-present key. keys[0] indexing assumes at least one selectable row exists after a successful poll (there is always the active window row).

pane_status PRECEDENCE (attention wins over working) must be order-INDEPENDENT: `s['status']=='attention' or (s['status']=='working' and pane_status.get(pane)!='attention')` (sidebar.py:1089). Attention always overwrites; working only fills if not already attention. Final map value is deterministic regardless of session iteration order — preserve that so parity does not depend on registry listing order.

QUIT MUST SHELL OUT: q/Q runs toggle via `tmux run-shell -b <toggle.sh>` then returns (sidebar.py:983-987). Running toggle logic in-process would kill this pane's own child. The Rust daemon must delegate teardown to the tmux server, not call its own toggle routine synchronously.

FOCUS-REPORTING LIFECYCLE: ESC[?1004h written on start, ESC[?1004l on exit via atexit (sidebar.py:912-921,937-938). Written with raw os.write to the stdout fd, bypassing curses. The OFF escape MUST fire on every exit incl. the loop's several `return`s and panics; a missed OFF leaves the user's terminal emitting focus reports. Do NOT special-case a bare ESC in the input path (comment 909-911): an arrow key after a focus report can fragment into ESC+'['+letter and swallowing ESC eats the key.

read_selection/write_selection use TAB-joined key tuples; read strips ONLY the trailing newline and treats an empty first field as None (sidebar.py:545-560). Do not trim tabs (a leading empty field would shift). Selection file is the shared cursor across all per-window sidebars.

Mouse: mouseinterval(0) + mask ALL_MOUSE_EVENTS; only BUTTON1_PRESSED|BUTTON1_CLICKED acts; getmouse() failure degrades to bstate=0,my=-1 (sidebar.py:996-1006). row_idx = mouse_y + offset; must bounds-check and require an actual dict item.

KEY_RESIZE has no explicit branch — input_detected marks the tick dirty and draw() recomputes offset/size from getmaxyx (comment 1007-1008). Width-sync also keys off getmaxyx()[1] each poll (sidebar.py:1047), so a resize is observed both as a repaint and as a possible width event.

focused_panes iterates ALL windows flagged active (sidebar.py:1079); a tmux session has exactly one active window, but the comprehension does not assume it. has_focus additionally requires this pane be the active pane of the active window AND sidebar_active (sidebar.py:1023) so only the truly-focused sidebar paints the selection bar; every other sidebar shows the shared selection without the reverse-video cursor.

Self-exit order matters: check no-windows -> me-None -> lower-numbered-sidebar -> no-real-panes, all BEFORE width sync and rows (sidebar.py:1015-1030). Reordering could resize/paint a window that is about to close.

functions.name: run
functions.behavior: Sidebar-mode entry point, equivalent to setlocale + curses.wrapper(main) (sidebar.py:924,1126-1128). Sets LC_ALL locale from env, brings up the terminal (raw/noecho/keypad/alt-screen) behind an RAII guard that restores it AND writes focus-reporting-off on any exit or panic, runs setup_terminal(), then loops via run_loop() until a self-exit condition returns. Resolves SIDEBAR_PANE from env TMUX_PANE (mandatory) and STATE_DIR from XDG_STATE_HOME or ~/.local/state joined with 'tmux-agent-wrangler'; derives REGISTRY/ATTENTION/WORKING/NOTIFIED/SELECTION_FILE/WIDTH_FILE paths under it (sidebar.py:29-42).
functions.side_effects: Terminal raw mode + alt screen; installs panic-safe restore+focus-off guard; reads env.
edge_cases: TMUX_PANE absent -> hard abort (Python KeyError on os.environ['TMUX_PANE']); the daemon must not run outside a tmux pane.
Empty XDG_STATE_HOME falls back to ~/.local/state (Python truthiness `or`).
Locale must be set before terminal init so braille spinner + '●' render at their true width.
Terminal restore must survive panics, not only clean returns (curses.wrapper parity).

functions.name: setup_terminal
functions.behavior: One-time init at loop start (sidebar.py:925-938): hide cursor; use_default_colors; start_color; allocate base UI pairs 1=green,2=cyan,3=yellow,4=red on the default (-1) background; call color::init_agent_colors() to allocate the per-Claude-color agent pairs starting at id 10; enable ALL_MOUSE_EVENTS with mouseinterval(0); turn focus reporting ON (proto: ESC[?1004h) and register focus-reporting-OFF for exit.
functions.side_effects: Mutates global curses color-pair table and mouse mode; writes ESC[?1004h to stdout fd (raw, bypassing curses).
edge_cases: init_pair may raise curses.error on a color-poor terminal; color::init_agent_colors already swallows per-name errors (color module), base pairs 1-4 are assumed to succeed as in Python.
mouseinterval(0) disables click-vs-drag timing so BUTTON1_CLICKED/PRESSED fire immediately; a Rust curses binding must replicate the zero interval.
Focus reporting only produces reports when the user set tmux `focus-events on`; without it the ON escape is harmless and the loop relies on the 1s poll (+ focus.sh C-l nudge).

functions.name: FocusGuard (set_focus_reporting)
functions.signature: struct FocusGuard; impl Drop for FocusGuard { fn drop(&mut self) { set_focus_reporting(false); } }  //  fn set_focus_reporting(enabled: bool)
functions.behavior: Writes DEC private mode 1004 enable/disable to the stdout fd: ESC[?1004h when enabled, ESC[?1004l when disabled (sidebar.py:912-921). Implemented as a raw fd write, deliberately NOT through the curses screen buffer. Modeled as an RAII guard so the OFF write is the Python atexit(set_focus_reporting, False) equivalent and fires on every exit path.
functions.side_effects: Raw byte write to stdout fd; best-effort (ignore write errors, like Python's except OSError: pass).
edge_cases: Write failures are swallowed silently.
Must not be routed through the curses refresh path (ordering/flush differs); use the fd directly as Python does.
The OFF escape must run exactly once per process lifetime on shutdown; ensure the guard is not accidentally dropped early or duplicated.

functions.name: run_loop
functions.signature: fn run_loop(term: &mut Term, st: &mut LoopState) -> ExitReason
functions.behavior: The fixed-cadence event loop (sidebar.py:975-1123). Each iteration: getch with TICK_MS(16ms) timeout; now=monotonic; input_detected = ch!=-1. On input, force a poll and dispatch via handle_input (may return Quit). Then run poll_step if force_poll|cached is None|elapsed>=POLL_INTERVAL(1.0). Then advance the animation frame if elapsed>=ANIM_INTERVAL(0.0625). Then build_and_reconcile if polled or (frame advanced and animating). Then compute dirty and draw. Returns when a self-exit/quit fires. Decouples input (16ms), data poll (1s), animation (~16fps), and repaint (only when dirty).
functions.side_effects: Drives all tmux queries, state-file IO, notifications, resize requests, and screen repaints indirectly via the steps it calls.
edge_cases: Constants are load-bearing: POLL_INTERVAL=1.0, ANIM_INTERVAL=0.0625, TICK_MS=16 (sidebar.py:950-952).
First iteration: force_poll=True and last_poll=last_frame=0.0 guarantee an immediate poll and a frame advance.
input_detected always forces a poll THIS tick (force_poll=True at 980) AND marks the tick dirty.
getch returns -1 on timeout (no input); any other value is input including KEY_RESIZE and mouse.
Poll gate also fires when cached is None (never-polled), independent of the timer.

functions.name: handle_input
functions.signature: fn handle_input(ch: i32, st: &mut LoopState, term: &Term) -> InputOutcome
functions.behavior: Dispatches one key/mouse event against the CURRENTLY on-screen rows/keys/items/offset from the previous build (sidebar.py:979-1008). q/Q: shell out `tmux run-shell -b <toggle.sh>` and signal Quit (never toggle in-process). Up/k: selected_key = keys[max(0, idx-1)] and write_selection. Down/j: keys[min(len-1, idx+1)] and write_selection. Enter/10/13: activate(items[idx]). Mouse: getmouse; if BUTTON1_PRESSED|CLICKED, row_idx=my+offset, and if that row is a dict item, set+write selection and activate it. Sets force_poll for the tick.
functions.side_effects: Writes selection file; runs tmux commands (select-window/select-pane via activate, run-shell via quit); no direct draw.
edge_cases: All branches gated on non-empty keys/rows/items; first tick (empty) is a no-op.
keys.index finds FIRST occurrence; selection keys are unique tuples.
Nav clamps at both ends (max/min), never wraps.
Mouse getmouse() error -> treat as bstate=0, my=-1 (no action).
KEY_RESIZE intentionally has no branch: it only marks the tick dirty so draw() recomputes from getmaxyx.
toggle.sh path is derived from the daemon binary's own location (Python uses dirname(abspath(__file__))).

functions.name: poll_step
functions.signature: fn poll_step(term: &Term, st: &mut LoopState) -> Result<PollOutcome, ExitReason>
functions.behavior: The 1s data poll (sidebar.py:1011-1094). Calls tmux::fetch_windows() -> (windows, pane_to_window, sidebars, pane_paths, pane_progress, pane_titles, pane_pids, sidebar_active). Runs check_self_exit (returns Exit on any of the 4 conditions). Computes has_focus = me.active && sidebar_active. Detects a pane-set change to arm relayout_grace=2. Runs the width-sync block (width module). Reads shared selection (overrides selected_key). Computes focused_panes (active pane of active window). Calls assoc::fetch_agent_sessions, then notify::notify_attention(sessions, bell_enabled(), osc_notify_mode()), then notify::acknowledge_focused_attention(sessions, focused_panes). Builds pane_status (attention-wins map). Reads hook_progress_enabled()/osc_progress_enabled(). Stores the 7-tuple `cached`=(windows,sessions,pane_progress,pane_status,hook_on,osc_on,has_focus) and marks polled=True.
functions.side_effects: Runs many tmux queries; may issue resize-pane; writes width/selection/notified files; rings bell / emits OSC notification; clears attention markers; reads all option values fresh each poll.
edge_cases: Order of the 4 self-exit checks is fixed and runs before any resize/paint (see parity risk).
read_selection overrides local selected_key every poll so all sidebars converge on the shared cursor.
notify runs BEFORE acknowledge so an event signals before focus clears its marker (comment 1081-1084).
Option-reading functions (bell/osc/hook/label/min/sync) are re-queried each poll, not cached, so live tmux option changes take effect within 1s (delegated to tmux/width/notify modules).
focused_panes uses a set comprehension over active windows' active panes; empty if the active window has no non-sidebar active pane.

functions.name: check_self_exit
functions.signature: fn check_self_exit(me: &Window, sidebars: &HashSet<PaneId>, windows_empty: bool, me_missing: bool) -> Option<ExitReason>
functions.behavior: The four singleton/liveness self-exit conditions inside the poll (sidebar.py:1015-1030): (1) fetch_windows returned no windows; (2) SIDEBAR_PANE not in pane_to_window (this pane vanished); (3) another sidebar pane in THIS window has a numerically lower pane id (spawn-race loser exits); (4) this window has no real (non-sidebar) panes left, so tmux should close the window. Any condition returns an Exit that unwinds the loop and triggers terminal restore + focus-off.
functions.side_effects: None (pure decision) beyond signaling process exit.
edge_cases: Pane-id compare is numeric on int(id[1:]) after stripping '%', not lexical.
Condition 3 skips SIDEBAR_PANE itself and only counts sidebars filed under `me`.
'no real panes' uses me.panes which fetch_windows already built EXCLUDING sidebar panes and this pane.
These checks are what make one-sidebar-per-window a hard invariant despite independent processes.

functions.name: build_and_reconcile
functions.behavior: Rebuilds the display model when needed (sidebar.py:1107-1117). Unpacks `cached`; if polled or (frame_advanced && animating), calls rows::build_rows(windows, sessions, pane_progress, pane_status, hook_on, osc_on, frame) to get rows; derives items = dict rows, keys = their keys; if selected_key not in keys, snaps it to the first active-window row's key else keys[0]; recomputes animating = any on-screen indicator glyph is in the braille spinner set. On idle ticks it does nothing, so rows/keys/items/animating persist and still match the screen for the next input tick.
functions.side_effects: None (pure model rebuild); mutates LoopState fields only.
edge_cases: `animating` is read from the PREVIOUS build to decide whether THIS tick rebuilds for a frame advance — the spinner-continuation feedback loop.
selected_key reconciliation runs only inside a build; between builds a stale selection persists.
keys[0] fallback assumes at least one selectable row after a poll (the active window row always exists).
The cached unpack itself is outside the build gate because it supplies has_focus to draw every tick (comment 1101-1107).

functions.name: compute_dirty_and_draw
functions.behavior: Decides whether to repaint and does so (sidebar.py:1119-1123). snapshot=(cached, selected_key); dirty = input_detected || (frame_advanced && animating) || snapshot != last_painted. On dirty, calls draw(stdscr, rows, selected_key, offset, has_focus) (rows/color module) which returns the possibly-adjusted scroll offset, and records last_painted=snapshot. Otherwise leaves the screen untouched, so an idle sidebar repaints no more than the poll cadence.
functions.side_effects: Screen repaint via draw(); updates offset and last_painted in LoopState.
edge_cases: snapshot != last_painted requires DEEP structural equality over the whole cached tuple + selection (see parity risk); a shallow/identity compare breaks it.
draw returns the clamped offset (scrolls to keep the selected row visible); the loop must feed it back into LoopState.offset.
A focus change alters has_focus inside cached, so snapshot differs and a repaint occurs without input.

functions.name: window_real_panes
functions.behavior: Lists a window's real (non-sidebar, non-self) pane ids via `tmux list-panes -t <win> -F '#{pane_id}\t#{@wrangler_sidebar}'`, excluding any pane flagged @wrangler_sidebar==1 and SIDEBAR_PANE itself (sidebar.py:780-786). Used by focus() to land focus on a real pane.
edge_cases: A pane with the sidebar flag unset but equal to SIDEBAR_PANE is still excluded (belt-and-braces).
Returns empty if the window is sidebar-only (focus() then leaves target_pane None).

functions.name: focus
functions.behavior: Focuses a window and optionally a specific pane (sidebar.py:789-801). If no pane given, it inspects the window's active pane; if that active pane is a sidebar (flag==1 or == SIDEBAR_PANE) it retargets to the first real pane from window_real_panes so focus never lands on a sidebar. Emits `tmux select-window -t <win>` plus, when a target pane resolved, `; select-pane -t <pane>` in one tmux invocation.
functions.side_effects: Changes tmux active window / active pane.
edge_cases: If the window is sidebar-only and no real pane exists, only select-window runs (no select-pane).
The two subcommands are chained in a single tmux call using the literal ';' argument, matching Python's cmds list.

functions.name: activate
functions.behavior: Thin dispatcher: focus(item.win.id, item.pane) (sidebar.py:804-805). Called on Enter and on a left mouse click on a selectable row. Window rows carry no pane (focus lands on a real pane); pane and agent rows carry the pane displaying the target.
edge_cases: Agent rows use the pane from the ("a", id, pane) key so clicking a session under one window focuses that window's copy, not another placement of the same session.

functions.name: cmd_tmux_entry
functions.behavior: Port of wrangler.tmux (the TPM load hook, wrangler.tmux:1-38). Binds @wrangler-key (default Tab) to the toggle subcommand and @wrangler-focus-key (default a) to the focus subcommand, both via `tmux bind-key`. If @wrangler-auto-install-hooks is truthy (on|1|yes|true), runs the hook installer in the background (`tmux run-shell -b`). Installs `after-new-window` and `after-break-pane` hooks that run the spawn subcommand with --if-active. Unsets the legacy `session-window-changed` hook. Patches automatic-rename-format to `#{?#{@wrangler_sidebar},#{window_name},<old>}` unless it already references @wrangler_sidebar, so focusing the sidebar pane (command 'Python' today) does not rename the window.
functions.side_effects: Runs many tmux bind-key/set-hook/set-option commands; optionally spawns the hook installer.
edge_cases: automatic-rename-format patch is idempotent (skips if already contains @wrangler_sidebar).
In Rust the sidebar command is no longer 'python3 .../sidebar.py' — the rename guard keys off the @wrangler_sidebar pane option, NOT the pane command, so it stays valid after the port.
Hook install is backgrounded so load never blocks and is safe to fire every load (idempotent).
Legacy session-window-changed unset must remain for users upgrading.

functions.name: cmd_toggle
functions.behavior: Port of toggle.sh (toggle.sh:1-20). Lists all panes server-wide flagged @wrangler_sidebar==1. If any exist, kills every one (best-effort, ignore failures) and exits — the OFF switch. Otherwise deletes the shared width file and spawns one sidebar per window by calling the spawn subcommand for each `#{window_id}` from `tmux list-windows`.
functions.side_effects: Kills sidebar panes OR removes STATE_DIR/width and spawns sidebars; server-wide.
edge_cases: kill-pane failures are swallowed (`|| true`).
Width file is cleared ONLY on turn-on so a fresh session starts at the default width, not a stale synced one.
The q/Q key and this command share the same teardown; q routes here via `tmux run-shell -b` so the server, not the dying pane, performs the kill.

functions.name: cmd_spawn
functions.signature: fn cmd_spawn(term: &Term, if_active: bool, win: Option<&str>) -> anyhow::Result<()>
functions.behavior: Port of spawn.sh (spawn.sh:1-32). Target window defaults to the current `#{window_id}`. With --if-active, no-op unless the session already has at least one @wrangler_sidebar pane (so the new-window hooks only auto-spawn when the sidebar is toggled on). No-op if the target window already has a sidebar pane. Otherwise reads @wrangler-width (default 32) and creates a detached, full-height, left-hand split of that width running the daemon in sidebar mode, then tags the new pane with `set-option -p @wrangler_sidebar 1`.
functions.side_effects: Creates a tmux pane running the sidebar daemon; sets the @wrangler_sidebar pane option (the singleton/registry marker).
edge_cases: --if-active gate and the per-window existing-sidebar gate are BOTH checked; either short-circuits to exit 0.
The split command must be `split-window -d -f -h -b -l <width>` and set the pane option immediately after so a racing spawn/self-exit sees the flag.
Even so, two spawns can race; the loser is culled later by check_self_exit's lower-numbered-pane rule, not by this command.
@wrangler-width default 32 differs from @wrangler-min-width default 24 (floor) — do not conflate.

functions.name: cmd_focus
functions.behavior: Port of focus.sh (focus.sh:1-15). Finds THIS window's sidebar pane (first pane with @wrangler_sidebar==1); if none, no-op (never spawns). Otherwise `select-pane -t <sidebar>` then `send-keys -t <sidebar> C-l` to force an immediate repaint, since select-pane delivers no input and the sidebar's blocking getch would otherwise sit until the next 1s poll before the focus highlight appears.
functions.side_effects: Selects the sidebar pane and injects a C-l keystroke into it.
edge_cases: No-op when the current window has no sidebar (sidebar toggled off for this window).
C-l is the guaranteed repaint path when the terminal/config has focus-events off so mode-1004 reports never arrive; the sidebar loop treats C-l (input_detected) as a redraw+forced poll.
Uses the @wrangler_sidebar option as the source of truth, never the pane command.
